# Decision History

Every feature this project has shipped through its specification process, condensed into
one story: what each set out to achieve, why it mattered, where later decisions undid or
refined an earlier one, and what we learned along the way. It favors judgment over
procedure — for step-by-step acceptance gates from before this process existed, read the
[development notes](../dev-notes/index.qmd); for the design of the system *as it stands
today*, read [architecture](../explanation/architecture.qmd) and [seams](../reference/seams.qmd).

Each feature now has its own page — this page is the map, one table per arc, plus the arc
narrative: the intros, transitions, and retrospectives that turn the entries into one
story. The twenty-four features fall into five arcs: the agent surface taking shape, the
AI plumbing industrializing, platform and delivery polish, trust, gates, and the
industrialized practice, and surface, reach, and the docs themselves. Within each arc the
entries flow chronologically; reversals are stated openly wherever they happened —
including several decisions that were built and then replaced inside their own feature
before landing. Contracts the narrative points at are preserved verbatim under
`appendices/`.

## Arc A — The agent surface takes shape

Mayon gained its first external tool, then rebuilt the surface where tool activity
appears. A web-search integration produced a flood of raw tool rows; typed timeline
entries made that flood legible; live use exposed what fixtures could not catch; and a
contract pass converged every assistant-initiated interaction into one governed place.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [001 — Brave Search MCP service](001-brave-search-mcp.qmd#sec-001) | standing — credential/topology design revised twice within the feature itself |
| [002 — Chat timeline kind model](002-chat-timeline-kinds.qmd#sec-002) | core standing — live-item placement superseded by 004 |

One day of live use against the new registry surfaced four defects no fixture caught —
the agenda for the next feature.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [003 — Timeline UX fixes](003-timeline-ux-fixes.qmd#sec-003) | standing |

With kinds, ordering, and pairing sound, the first real MCP server — whose risky calls
need human approval — exposed honesty gaps that only a contract-level pass could close.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [004 — Internal area unification](004-internal-area-unification.qmd#sec-004) | contracts standing — result-body presentation superseded by 005 |

That collapse fix also exposed the next gap: hiding the payload was easy, but whatever
appeared on expand still read like a wall.

*Arc A in retrospect:* the surface learned to tell the truth in layers — first structural
truth (typed entries), then behavioral truth (ordering, pairing), then contractual truth
(where interaction may live and what diagnostics may say). Every later arc inherited those
contracts instead of rediscovering them.

## Arc B — The AI plumbing industrializes

Results learned to render by shape rather than server identity, bespoke UI gave way to
adopted community patterns, provider onboarding turned into catalog data, request
behavior centralized into one resolution seam, and study controls opened up without
touching fragile geometry.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [005 — Shape-driven tool result rendering](005-shape-driven-results.qmd#sec-005) | standing |
| [006 — AI elements adoption](006-ai-elements-adoption.qmd#sec-006) | standing |

With the interaction surface settled, the same industrializing instinct turned to the
provider side of the wire — where manual endpoint entry had become the bottleneck.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [007 — First-class inference provider templates](007-inference-provider-templates.qmd#sec-007) | standing |
| [008 — First-class inference router templates](008-inference-router-templates.qmd#sec-008) | standing |

Direct providers and routers could now be added without code — but the parameters each
request carried were still hard-coded and, for newer models, broken.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [009 — Provider request settings](009-provider-request-settings.qmd#sec-009) | standing |

Study controls were the last feature-boundary piece still decided unilaterally by the app;
opening them up safely meant working next to some of the most fragile geometry in the
codebase.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [010 — Customizable expound instructions](010-custom-expound-instructions.qmd#sec-010) | standing |

*Arc B in retrospect:* every entry traded ad-hoc branching for data, derivation, or
adoption — shapes over identities, catalogs over code, one resolver over scattered maps,
user-managed strings over constants. Notably, the arc shipped almost entirely additive to
Arc A's contracts, validating them as a stable foundation. The one deep rewrite —
request-settings resolution — earned its deletion by replacing code the dialect research
proved defective.

## Arc C — Platform & delivery polish

This arc widened who can install Mayon and made the product legible at a glance —
and both features carry decision reversals handled the way we now consider standard:
built, evidenced, reviewed, and calmly revised.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [011 — Podman compatibility](011-podman-support.qmd#sec-011) | standing — one same-session scope reversal |
| [012 — UI visual articulation pass](012-ui-visual-articulation.qmd#sec-012) | standing — three mid-flight reversals landed before merge |

*Arc C in retrospect:* neither feature moved a schema; both changed how much of the system
users can see and steer. The repeated pattern — build the strong form, capture evidence,
let an explicit ruling trim it — is the project's decisive-method matured: reversals
stopped being failures once they stopped being expensive.

## Arc D — Trust, gates & the industrialized practice

By late August the practice itself became the feature. The specification archive — twelve
feature directories and 133,926 words — was consolidated into the decision history you
are reading, kept honest by a fixed template, fixed budgets, and an audit-to-green gate
before any deletion. Mayon went onto the public internet behind one authentication gate
enforced once at the server seam, its uniformity proven by a CI sweep test rather than
per-route discipline. The chat experience gained an end-to-end suite driven by a
protocol-exact mock LLM — no live provider, no API key, zero product diff. The freshly
public repository gained always-on, report-only security posture detection. And the
manual release-candidate pass became automated verification: the mock learned to
discriminate request kinds and grade deterministically while a real browser drove the
real app.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [013 — Consolidate spec history](013-consolidate-spec-history.qmd) | standing — its one-page form now split into these per-feature pages |
| [017 — Secure public launch](017-secure-public-launch.qmd) | standing |
| [017 — Mock-LLM chat test suite](017-mock-llm-chat-tests.qmd) | standing — extended by 020 — RC UI verification |
| [019 — Security posture detection](019-security-posture-detection.qmd) | standing — the push-protection enforcement gap is a recorded follow-up |
| [020 — RC UI verification](020-rc-ui-verification.qmd) | standing |

*Arc D in retrospect:* trust was made structural, never per-route discipline — one hook
covers every endpoint and a sweep test keeps it one; deletion waited on audit gates going
green; and "enabled" in a settings API counted only after live adversarial tests proved
it enforcing, with the degraded leg accepted and recorded rather than papered over. The
arc legislated its own restraint too: report-only detection, no scheduled update floods,
and gates that never block on unproven signal — a solo maintainer's noise budget treated
as a design constraint. Splitting this history into per-feature pages is the same
discipline applied to itself.

## Arc E — Surface, reach & the docs themselves

The final arc widened what the surface can do and how far the product reaches — and made
the docs themselves into a shipped feature. Settings gained navigation around a
deliberately frozen page; a six-card idea deck traded the fully designed floating reply
outline for its leaner sibling, the section peek strip, which shipped the panel's contract
primitives instead of forking them; GitHub Copilot brought the workplace main AI onboard
as the first provider kind defined by auth rather than wire format; image chat parts gave
vision a parts-based contract under which voice, video, and files become follow-on slices
rather than a rewrite; branched chats learned to push their outcomes back into the parent
as anchored artifacts; and the documentation was restructured into the Diátaxis website
this page is published on.

| Feature | Status |
| --- | --- |
| [014 — Settings page navigation](014-settings-navigation.qmd) | standing |
| [015 — Floating reply outline](015-floating-reply-outline.qmd) | designed, not built — contract primitives shipped via the section peek strip |
| [016 — GitHub Copilot support](016-github-copilot-support.qmd) | standing |
| [017 — Section peek strip](017-section-peek-strip.qmd) | standing — an owner ruling reshaped it into a page-level tick gutter |
| [018 — Image chat parts](018-image-chat-parts.qmd) | standing — voice, video, and files stay recorded future work |
| [019 — Diátaxis docs website](019-diataxis-docs-website.qmd) | standing |
| [020 — Branch back-propagation](020-branch-backprop.qmd) | standing — merged to main, not yet in a tagged release |

*Arc E in retrospect:* reach arrived without rewrites — a new modality became a nullable
parts column beside canonical text, a new provider became a kind behind the existing
keystore and resolver, and branch back-propagation became one more entry kind in the model
[002 — Chat timeline kind model](002-chat-timeline-kinds.qmd#sec-002) built, riding
abstractions earlier arcs had already paid for. It is also the record's most honest
stretch: 015 was fully designed and never built, its contract realized by a sibling that
consumed it, the floating panel kept on the books as the recorded upgrade path — declined
winners recorded as upgrade paths, not dead ends.

## Where the story stands

Twenty-four features in three weeks of calendar time, with one recurring shape: invent
narrowly, prove broadly, revise without ceremony. The durable mechanics — typed entries,
derived states, written contracts, catalog-driven extensibility, offset-sanctified
selection, evidenced styling rulings — now function as the platform every future feature
inherits. Arcs D and E hardened and widened that platform: releases ship through
automated gates driven by a protocol-exact mock, the product sits behind one centrally
enforced authentication gate with always-on security posture detection, reach grew
through Copilot, image parts, and branch back-propagation, and the documentation became
the Diátaxis website you are reading. Not everything is built, and the record says so:
the floating reply outline remains what a where-am-I marker on the strip would grow into;
voice, video, and file support stay recorded as future work, not abandoned; and push
protection's enforcement gap is a recorded follow-up. The know-how distilled here is
deliberately opinionated; when a future change contradicts an entry here, update that
entry in the same change — this history is a living decision record, not a museum.
